name: Intake
tagline: A hosted form tool for collecting structured intake: build a form, share a link, get submissions in one place.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Public detail on this one is thin, so treat the specifics as unverified, but the shape is familiar: a form builder, a shareable public link, and a submissions inbox. That shape is one of the most reliably clonable things in software, because the hard part is a schema editor and a table, not distribution or data. An agent will give you field types, validation, a public form page, and a local submissions list in a single session. The weekend creeps in once you want file uploads, email notifications that actually land, spam filtering, and a link you can hand to a paying client without wincing. Nothing here is a moat, it is just a pile of small chores someone else already did.
coreLoopDIY: Define a form's fields in a small admin UI, publish it at a public URL, and collect validated submissions into a local database you can read and export.
requirements: Node 20 and a place to run it, local or a cheap VPS
SQLite file, no managed database needed
An email API key (Resend or SMTP) if you want new-submission notifications
An S3-compatible bucket if you want file upload fields
A domain or tunnel if the form link goes to clients
whatYouLose: Email deliverability that is someone else's problem instead of yours
Spam and bot filtering, which you will not notice you need until the first flood
Polished, mobile-correct form rendering and conditional logic that does not feel bolted on
Integrations out of the box: Slack, Zapier, calendar, CRM handoff
Someone else's uptime on the one URL your clients use to reach you
moatNotes: Form products compete on how little the form makes you think, which is real work but not a moat you cannot cross with taste and a weekend.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the form is a client-facing surface, and client-facing surfaces are where cheap self-hosting bites. Paying means the link never 404s during a holiday, the notification email lands in a real inbox, the mobile layout is already correct, and the uploads do not quietly fail at 12MB. For a freelancer billing real money per project, that is a trivially justified line item against an afternoon of debugging multipart uploads.
notes: The clone is easy; the trust in the link you paste into a client email is the part you are actually buying.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted client intake form tool. Stack: Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Drizzle for schema. No external auth provider, no analytics, no telemetry.

In scope:
1. A single-admin area protected by one password from ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env, stored in an httpOnly signed cookie. No user accounts, no signup.
2. Admin can create forms. Each form has a title, an intro blurb, a slug, and an ordered list of fields.
3. Field types: short text, long text, email, number, single select, multi select, date, checkbox. Each field has a label, help text, and a required flag. Store the field list as JSON on the form row.
4. A drag-to-reorder field editor. Keep it plain: list rows with up/down buttons are acceptable, do not pull in a drag library.
5. Public form page at /f/[slug]. Server-render it, validate on the server with Zod built dynamically from the stored field list, show per-field errors, and show a thank-you state on success.
6. Submissions stored in a submissions table with form id, JSON answers, created_at, and user agent. Admin can view a form's submissions in a table, open a single submission, and export all of them as CSV.
7. Optional email notification on new submission via Resend, using RESEND_API_KEY and NOTIFY_EMAIL from .env. If either is missing, skip sending silently and log once.
8. Basic spam defense: a honeypot field, a minimum time-on-page check, and a per-IP rate limit of 10 submissions per hour held in SQLite.

Out of scope, do not build: file uploads, conditional logic, payments, multi-user teams, webhooks, themes, embeds.

Deliverables: a seed script that creates one example form, a README with setup and deploy notes, .env.example listing every variable, and the SQLite file path configurable via DATABASE_URL. Make npm run dev work from a clean clone with only ADMIN_PASSWORD set.
